skill.name: document-generation
skill.description: Generate Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and PDF documents from structured content and simple HTML inputs.
skill.summary: Creates common Office documents and extracts PDF text for document automation workflows.
skill.author: BOHUYESHAN-APB

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, CSS text, comments, or routine output directory handling. The real risks are unvalidated remote image downloads in Word and PowerPoint generation, plus unsanitized output filenames that can escape intended output directories.

remediation.issue: Remote image URLs are fetched during Word and PowerPoint generation without network policy controls.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict image fetching to approved schemes and hosts, block private network ranges, enforce timeouts, verify content type, and cap response size.

remediation.issue: Output filenames can escape the configured output directory.
remediation.suggestion: Accept only safe basenames, reject absolute paths and parent directory segments, and verify resolved paths remain under the output directory before writing.

remediation.issue: Temporary image files may remain on disk after PowerPoint image handling errors.
remediation.suggestion: Use a try/finally cleanup block or a temporary directory context so downloaded image files are removed after any failure.

content.user_title: Generate Office Documents from Structured Content
content.value_statement: Teams often need repeatable Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and PDF files from structured content. This skill provides Python document generators for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
actual_capabilities: Generates DOCX documents from HTML with headings, paragraphs, lists, tables, inline styles, and images.
Creates PPTX presentations from slide-oriented HTML with titles, text blocks, tables, charts, and images.
Exports spreadsheet rows from a list of dictionaries into XLSX files.
Renders HTML or plain text content into PDF documents using WeasyPrint.
Extracts text from PDF files and converts Markdown into HTML for downstream generation.
limitations: PDF extraction is implemented, but Word, PowerPoint, and Excel extraction are not implemented in the scripts.
Remote image fetching needs network safety controls before use with untrusted HTML.
Generated layouts are basic and may need manual review for complex branding or dense content.
Filename inputs should be sanitized by the caller until the skill enforces path containment.

use_cases.title: Generate Client Reports
use_cases.description: Create Word or PDF reports from prepared HTML sections, tables, and summary text.

use_cases.title: Build Presentation Drafts
use_cases.description: Turn structured slide content into a PowerPoint deck with titles, text, tables, charts, and images.

use_cases.title: Export Operational Data
use_cases.description: Convert row-based business data into an Excel workbook for review, handoff, or reporting.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Document
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a simple Word or PDF output.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Word document from this content. Use clear headings, short paragraphs, and a simple table for any structured data I provide.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Slide Deck
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for a presentation from an outline.
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this outline into a PowerPoint deck. Use one main idea per slide, concise bullet points, and tables only where they improve comparison.

prompt_templates.title: Export Data to Excel
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Excel file from these rows. Preserve the column names, keep values readable, and use a filename that contains only letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores.

prompt_templates.title: Produce a Report Package
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request combining multiple output formats.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a report package with a DOCX narrative, a PDF copy, a PPTX executive summary, and an XLSX data appendix from the supplied source material.

output_examples.input: A project status outline with milestones, risks, owners, and next steps.
output_examples.output: A Word report with section headings, a risk table, owner assignments, and a concise action summary.

output_examples.input: A sales briefing with three product messages, market data, and a comparison table.
output_examples.output: A PowerPoint deck with title slides, message slides, a data chart, and a comparison table formatted for review.

output_examples.input: A list of monthly support metrics with categories, counts, and notes.
output_examples.output: An Excel workbook containing the provided rows as columns and records for analysis or sharing.

best_practices: Provide structured source content with clear headings, tables, and image references before generation.
Use safe filenames without path separators, parent directory segments, or user-specific secrets.
Review generated documents for layout quality, brand fit, and external image references before sharing.
anti_patterns: Do not pass untrusted HTML that contains arbitrary remote image URLs without network controls.
Do not use this skill as a secure file conversion sandbox for unknown documents.
Do not rely on the README extraction claims for Word, PowerPoint, or Excel files without adding those processors.

faq.question: Which document formats can this skill generate?
faq.answer: It can generate DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, and PDF files through Python scripts.

faq.question: Can it extract text from uploaded documents?
faq.answer: It includes PDF text extraction. The current scripts do not implement extraction for Word, PowerPoint, or Excel files.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Can it include images in generated documents?
faq.answer: Yes. Word and PowerPoint generation can add local images and remote image URLs, but remote URLs need safety controls.

faq.question: What inputs produce the best results?
faq.answer: Simple HTML, Markdown converted to HTML, structured rows, and concise outlines produce the most reliable output.

faq.question: Is it safe to use with untrusted content?
faq.answer: Use caution. Validate filenames and restrict remote URL fetching before processing untrusted content.
